    ['provider_zip_code', 'provider_id', 'average_covered_charges', 'average_total_payments', 'average_medicare_payments']

# Write to target CSV file
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_81/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source table
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_81/training_0.csv", index_col=0)

# Select only needed columns and rename to match target schema exactly
df = source0[['provider_zip_code', 'provider_id', 'average_covered_charges', 'average_total_payments', 'average_medicare_payments']]

# provider_zip_code is integer in target, ensure type
df['provider_zip_code'] = df['provider_zip_code'].astype(int)

# provider_id is float in target, ensure type
df['provider_id'] = df['provider_id'].astype(float)

# Group by provider_zip_code (primary key) and aggregate other columns by taking first value
# This ensures uniqueness and matches target key constraints
result = df.groupby('provider_zip_code', as_index=False).agg({
    'provider_id': 'first',
    'average_covered_charges': 'first',
    'average_total_payments': 'first',
    'average_medicare_payments': 'first'
})

# Write output to target file
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_81/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
